title: The registry sees settings only through the four-method ProviderSettings protocol
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Core/Models/ProviderSettings.swift:6-12 protocol ProviderSettings - isEnabled, binaryPath(for:), lastModel(for:), apiKey(for:); MainActor, AnyObject
action: The registry is constructed with a settings object.
expected_result: The registry can call exactly these four methods and nothing else on settings. It never writes settings back.
failure_cases: None.
windows_path: The same four-method interface, so the registry stays testable without the full settings store.
verification_method: unit with a stub settings object

title: A provider is enabled unless its rawValue is present in the persisted disabledProviders array
source_evidence: DroppyCode/App/AppSettings.swift:138 Key.disabledProviders - the defaults key is the literal "disabledProviders"
DroppyCode/App/AppSettings.swift:869-871 isEnabled - returns !disabledProviders.contains(provider.rawValue)
DroppyCode/App/AppSettings.swift:737 - loaded with defaults.stringArray(forKey:) defaulting to the empty array
action: Any caller asks whether a provider is enabled.
expected_result: Enablement is opt-out: every provider is enabled by default because the stored array starts empty. Only a rawValue present in the array disables that provider.
persistence: Persisted under the exact key "disabledProviders" as an array of provider rawValue strings.
failure_cases: A value that is not a known rawValue is retained in the array and simply never matches.
windows_path: Same key name and same opt-out semantics in the Windows settings store, so an imported profile keeps working.
verification_method: restart test: disable a provider, relaunch, confirm it is still disabled

title: Toggling the provider switch removes then conditionally appends the rawValue, so order changes and duplicates cannot accumulate
source_evidence: DroppyCode/App/AppSettings.swift:873-876 setEnabled - removeAll matching the rawValue, then append only when the new value is false
DroppyCode/App/AppSettings.swift:490-491 - the didSet writes the whole array back to defaults
action: The user flips a provider's switch.
expected_result: Enabling removes every occurrence of the rawValue. Disabling removes every occurrence and then appends exactly one, so the disabled provider moves to the end of the array. The whole array is written to defaults on each change.
failure_cases: None; the operation is total.
windows_path: Same array mutation and same write-through.
verification_method: unit asserting array contents and ordering after a toggle sequence

title: A custom binary path is stored per provider under providerBinaryPaths, trimmed, with an empty value removing the entry
source_evidence: DroppyCode/App/AppSettings.swift:137 Key.binaryPaths - the literal "providerBinaryPaths"
DroppyCode/App/AppSettings.swift:860-867 binaryPath(for:) and setBinaryPath - returns the empty string when absent; the setter trims whitespace and newlines and stores nil for an empty result
DroppyCode/App/AppSettings.swift:488-489 - the didSet writes the whole dictionary back
DroppyCode/App/AppSettings.swift:736 - loaded with defaults.dictionary(forKey:) cast to [String: String]
action: The user types in the Binary path field.
expected_result: Every keystroke that differs from the stored value writes the trimmed value under the provider rawValue in the dictionary keyed "providerBinaryPaths". Clearing the field removes the key entirely rather than storing an empty string.

windows_path: Same key and same trim-and-remove semantics; the value is a Windows path.

title: The last model used per provider is stored under lastModels and is the first choice of defaultModel
source_evidence: DroppyCode/App/AppSettings.swift:139 Key.models - the literal "lastModels"
DroppyCode/App/AppSettings.swift:878-879 lastModel(for:) - reads lastModels by rawValue
DroppyCode/App/AppSettings.swift:886-888 remember(model:effort:for:) - writes both lastModels and lastEfforts

title: API keys live in four Keychain items under one service, with UserDefaults holding a copy only when the Keychain refuses
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/APIKeychain.swift:29-33 setKey - kSecClassGenericPassword with kSecAttrService = AppInfo.name and kSecAttrAccount = the account string
DroppyCode/Services/Providers/DeepSeekKeychain.swift - account "DeepSeek API Key"
DroppyCode/Services/Providers/MetaKeychain.swift - account "Meta API Key"
DroppyCode/Services/Providers/ZaiKeychain.swift - account "Z.ai API Key"
DroppyCode/Services/Providers/CommandCodeKeychain.swift - account "Command Code API Key"
DroppyCode/App/AppSettings.swift:359-398 - each input didSet calls setAPIKey and then storeAPIKeyFallback with the empty string when the Keychain kept it
DroppyCode/App/AppSettings.swift:151-154 - the fallback defaults keys are deepseekAPIKey, metaAPIKey, zaiAPIKey, commandcodeAPIKey
preconditions: The user edits an API key field.
action: setAPIKeyInput is called for that provider.
expected_result: The key is trimmed of whitespace and newlines and written as a generic password under the app service name with one of exactly these four account strings: "DeepSeek API Key", "Meta API Key", "Z.ai API Key", "Command Code API Key". Accessibility is kSecAttrAccessibleWhenUnlocked. An empty key deletes the item. When the Keychain write returns false, and only then, the plaintext value is written to the matching UserDefaults key; when it succeeds the empty string is stored there, which removes the key.
side_effects: A Keychain delete followed by an add on every write; optionally a defaults write.
persistence: Keychain service = the app display name, four fixed account strings. Fallback defaults keys: deepseekAPIKey, metaAPIKey, zaiAPIKey, commandcodeAPIKey.
failure_cases: Keychain unavailable: SecItemAdd returns non-success, setKey returns false and the plaintext fallback is written.
windows_path: PLATFORM BOUNDARY: the Windows SecretStore must keep the same one-container-many-accounts partitioning and the same four account strings verbatim, because MCP secrets share the container and are distinguished only by account string. The plaintext fallback must be reconsidered explicitly rather than transliterated, since it writes a secret to disk.
verification_method: restart test on each of the four accounts plus a contract fixture on the account strings

title: apiKey(for:) prefers the stored trimmed key and falls back to the provider env var, returning the empty string for providers that accept no key
source_evidence: DroppyCode/App/AppSettings.swift:895-907 apiKey(for:) - reads the Keychain lazily, trims the stored input, returns it when non-empty, otherwise reads apiKeyEnvVar from the login environment and trims it; a provider with acceptsAPIKey false or a nil env var returns the empty string
action: The registry asks settings for a provider API key.
expected_result: Order is: stored input trimmed, then the environment variable trimmed, then the empty string. The Keychain is read at most once per run, on the first such call.
side_effects: Up to four Keychain reads on the first call.
failure_cases: Keychain read fails: the UserDefaults fallback value is used, or the empty string.
windows_path: Same order. The environment comes from the Windows process and registry environment. Platform boundary: environment capture and secret store.
verification_method: unit with injected store and environment

source_evidence: DroppyCode/App/AppSettings.swift:914-921 apiKeyInput(for:) - returns the raw stored input for the four providers and the empty string for the rest

title: Editing an API key field saves it and schedules a 600 millisecond debounced re-check, cancelling any pending one
source_evidence: DroppyCode/App/Views/Settings/SettingsView.swift:768-779 onChange(of: apiKey) - an edit only counts when the value differs from the stored input; then setAPIKeyInput, keyCheck?.cancel(), and a task that sleeps 600 milliseconds, checks Task.isCancelled, then calls refresh(provider) and loadCatalog(provider, force: true)
preconditions: The provider has acceptsAPIKey true and the field value differs from the stored input.
action: The user types or pastes into the API key field.
expected_result: The value is stored immediately. Any in-flight debounce task is cancelled. After exactly 600 milliseconds of no further edits, refresh(provider) runs, then loadCatalog(provider, force: true). Loading the stored key into the field on appear does not trigger this, because the guard compares against the stored input.
side_effects: Network validation call for the API-key providers; a CLI launch for Command Code.
persistence: The key is persisted immediately, before the debounce elapses.
failure_cases: The task is cancelled by a further edit or by the section disappearing: the check does not run and no status changes.
cancellation: The debounce task is explicitly cancelled on the next edit and the cancellation is checked after the sleep before any work.
windows_path: Same 600 millisecond debounce and the same cancel-then-replace pattern.
verification_method: interaction test with a fake clock asserting exactly one check after a burst of keystrokes

title: The API key field is re-synced from settings when the stored value changes elsewhere
source_evidence: DroppyCode/App/Views/Settings/SettingsView.swift:780-783 onChange(of: model.settings.apiKeyInput(for: provider)) - when the stored value differs from the field, the field is set from the store
preconditions: The section is on screen and the provider has acceptsAPIKey true.
action: The stored key changes from outside this field.
expected_result: The field takes the new value. The guard prevents a feedback loop with the edit handler because each side only acts when the two differ.
failure_cases: None.
windows_path: Same two-way guard.
verification_method: interaction test

title: The Binary path field loads from settings on appear and writes back on every differing change
source_evidence: DroppyCode/App/Views/Settings/SettingsView.swift:752-755 onAppear - binaryPath is filled from settings; the API key is filled only when acceptsAPIKey
DroppyCode/App/Views/Settings/SettingsView.swift:764-767 onChange(of: binaryPath) - writes through setBinaryPath when the value differs from the stored one
action: The section appears, or the user edits the Binary path field.
expected_result: On appear the field shows the stored custom path, or is empty. Each differing change writes through immediately. There is no debounce and no re-check: changing the binary path does NOT re-probe the provider until the refresh button is used or the app is relaunched.
failure_cases: A path that does not exist is still stored; the provider then reads as not installed on the next refresh.
windows_path: Same behavior, including the absence of an automatic re-probe.
verification_method: interaction test asserting no probe is spawned on a binary path edit

title: A custom binary path is resolved through the same lookup as the bare name, and a custom path that does not resolve disables the fallback candidates
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/ProviderRegistry.swift:216-223 executable(for:) - the custom path is passed to LoginEnvironment.which; on failure, a non-empty custom path returns nil instead of trying the fallbacks

DroppyCode/Core/Support/Shell.swift:411-423 which - a name containing a slash is expanded for a leading tilde and tested for executability; otherwise PATH is split on colon and each directory joined with the name
preconditions: A custom binary path is stored for a non API-key provider.
action: executable(for:) is called.
expected_result: The custom string is resolved with the same which() rule: containing a separator it is treated as a path with tilde expansion, otherwise it is searched on PATH. If it does not resolve, the function returns nil WITHOUT consulting fallbackExecutables. Only an empty custom path reaches the fallback list.
failure_cases: Custom path set but unresolvable: nil, so the section shows Not installed and the Install row, even though a bare-name copy exists on PATH.
windows_path: PLATFORM BOUNDARY: the is-a-path test must also accept backslash and a drive prefix, PATH must split on semicolon, and the execute-bit test must become a PATHEXT-aware existence test.
verification_method: contract fixture over a synthetic filesystem and PATH

title: Copilot falls back to the copilot binary inside the gh data directory when it is not on PATH
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/ProviderRegistry.swift:225-234 fallbackExecutables(.copilot) - GH_DATA_DIR when non-empty, else XDG_DATA_HOME with "gh" appended, else the home directory with ".local/share/gh" appended; then "copilot/copilot" is appended
DroppyCode/Services/Providers/ProviderRegistry.swift:222 - only candidates that pass the executable-file test are accepted
preconditions: Copilot is not on PATH and no custom binary path is set.
action: executable(for:) is called for Copilot.
expected_result: Exactly one candidate is produced, from the first of GH_DATA_DIR, XDG_DATA_HOME plus gh, or home plus .local/share/gh, with copilot/copilot appended. An empty environment value is treated as absent. The candidate is used only if it is an executable file.
failure_cases: Not executable or absent: executable(for:) returns nil.
windows_path: PLATFORM BOUNDARY: the gh CLI stores its data elsewhere on Windows, and the source gives no Windows location, so the equivalent directory must be established by probing rather than guessed. The three-step environment precedence should be preserved.
verification_method: contract fixture with a synthetic gh data directory

title: Command Code falls back to three alternate names on PATH and then to ten fixed directory-plus-name combinations
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/ProviderRegistry.swift:235-248 fallbackExecutables(.commandcode) - first LoginEnvironment.which for "command-code", "commandcode" and "cmd" in that order, appending each hit; then for each of the five directories HOME/.local/bin, /opt/homebrew/bin, /usr/local/bin, HOME/.npm-global/bin, HOME/.volta/bin, and each of the two names "command-code" and "cmd", a candidate is appended
preconditions: Command Code is not resolvable under the bare name cmd and no custom path is set.
action: executable(for:) is called for Command Code.
expected_result: The candidate list is built in exactly that order: up to three PATH hits first, then the ten directory-and-name combinations in directory-major, name-minor order. The first candidate that is an executable file wins.
side_effects: Up to three PATH walks plus ten existence tests.
failure_cases: Nothing found: nil.
windows_path: PLATFORM BOUNDARY: all five directories are Unix locations with no Windows meaning, and the "cmd" name collides with the Windows interpreter. The alternate-name list and its order are source facts and should be preserved; the directory list needs a probed Windows equivalent and must not be transliterated.
verification_method: contract fixture asserting candidate ordering
